reconcile.connective: Commentators read Jeremiah's "childless" as dynastic, not literal — barring Jeconiah's descendants from David's throne, not denying he had children at all.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells's Skeptic's Annotated Bible juxtaposes the texts flatly: Jeremiah bars all Jeconiah's seed from David's throne, yet Matthew traces the messianic line through him.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "Was Jeconiah Childless?" (online, c. 2000-)

excerpts.excerpt_text: Jeconiah was not actually without offspring (compare Jer 22:28, "his seed"; Ch1 3:17-18; Mat 1:12), but he was to be "written childless," as a warning to posterity, that is, without a lineal heir to his throne.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly reconciles all three cited passages (Jer 22:28-30, 1 Chr 3:17-18, Matt 1:12) in one sentence by reading 'childless' as barred-from-the-throne, not offspring-less.

pd_work.resource: John W. Haley, An Examination of the Alleged Discrepancies of the Bible (1875)
pd_work.author: John W. Haley
pd_work.note: Haley treats this exact pairing directly: 'Jehoiachin, father of Salathiel. He was "childless." Matt. i. 12. Jer. xxii. 30' -- explaining childless as 'with reference to a lineal successor.'
